{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRCof88AAAABZeMnqQ", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn7ElzhDFZEQ", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn7El", "number": 63, "title": "Implement 8259A OCW3 polling with normal EOI and PC-98 cascade handling", "body": "## Problem

Guests cannot acknowledge interrupts through 8259A software polling while CPU interrupts are disabled. `Pic::write` ignores OCW3.P, and `Pic::read` always returns ordinary status. Slave requests also reach master IR7 only inside `Bus::irq()`, which the CPU does not call with IF clear.

This is a bounded missing interrupt-controller behavior affecting both VM and Ap. It builds on the existing priority, EOI and special-mask implementation without requiring protected execution.

## Expected outcome

Implement normal-EOI (`ICW4.AEOI=0`) polling through the existing master and slave PIC ports, including two-stage acknowledgement of the fixed PC-98 cascade.

### Hardware contract

OCW3.P (bit 2; command `0Ch`) arms a single read acknowledgement. Return bit 7 indicates an eligible request; bits 2:0 identify its controller-local level, independently of the vector base. A successful poll clears the selected IRR bit and sets its ISR bit. Empty polls acknowledge nothing; use zero for unspecified result bits as a documented emulator policy. Selection respects masks, current priority and ISR blocking, including existing special-mask behavior. Freeze interrupt selection between the poll write and read, retaining later requests for subsequent service. Polling takes precedence over combined status-read commands. Further acknowledgements require fresh poll commands. The guest disables CPU interrupts; polling does not itself suppress INT. These semantics come from [Intel 8259A, Figure 8, Poll Command, Reading Status and Figure 9, printed pp. 13–17](https://courses.cs.washington.edu/courses/cse451/25wi/documentation/8259A.pdf#page=13).

Within the repository's fixed cascade wiring, master polling acknowledges IR7 only. Software separately polls the slave and issues each controller's EOI. Propagate slave interrupt transitions without requiring CPU acknowledgement, preserving deferred requests and avoiding duplicate cascade requests.

### Scope and remaining work

Include normal-EOI polling, its interaction with existing priority/SMM behavior, cascade propagation, initialization and reset. Keep changes within the existing device/bus design.

Polling with AEOI/automatic rotation and concurrent CPU acknowledgement while a poll is armed remain outside this Issue's verified scope. PIC also remains partial pending general ICW sequencing/SNGL/ICW3 configuration, alternate routing, SFNM, broader level-trigger behavior and spurious-interrupt fidelity. Protected execution, paging and basic x87 remain required project work. No unrelated UI, tooling redesign or commercial compatibility claim belongs here.

## Context and reproduction

Baseline inspected: `d3b0c3f3c422e395760e89b65162455e48c6207d`.

- [PIC implementation](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/d3b0c3f3c422e395760e89b65162455e48c6207d/src/devices.rs#L3): polling has no state or read-side acknowledgement.
- [Bus cascade](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/d3b0c3f3c422e395760e89b65162455e48c6207d/src/bus.rs#L358): slave-to-master propagation occurs inside `irq()`.
- [CPU interrupt delivery](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/d3b0c3f3c422e395760e89b65162455e48c6207d/src/cpu.rs#L617): `irq()` is conditional on IF and the interrupt shadow.
- [Existing PIC tests](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/d3b0c3f3c422e395760e89b65162455e48c6207d/tests/pic.rs) cover priority, SMM, cascade and source-built native guests, but contain no polling tests. Issues #41 and #43 implemented distinct OCW2/SMM behavior; the supplied open-Issue list is empty.

Minimal original reproduction to add before production edits:

```rust
let mut p = Pic::new(8);
p.write(true, 0);
p.request(1);
p.write(false, 0x0c);
assert_eq!(p.read(false), 0x81);
assert_eq!((p.irr, p.isr), (0, 2));
```

Source inspection predicts ordinary IRR readback `02h` and unchanged ISR on the baseline. This evaluator did not execute the reproduction or any builds/tests.

Project progress: RTC is partial following #61/#62. The supplied Coordinator report and [validation record](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/d3b0c3f3c422e395760e89b65162455e48c6207d/docs/validation.md#issue-61-ap-calendar-reads-2026-10-24) report 255 native integration and 92 production-Wasm browser passes. Those are attributed results, not evaluator execution. All 26 inventory categories and their full scopes remain retained: 22 partial, IDE/GRCG implemented_unverified, and paging/FPU unimplemented. No category is upgraded by this planning step.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] Record the minimal reproduction failing before production edits and passing afterward.
- [ ] Add original Rust tests in `tests/pic.rs` covering every request level and priority origin, empty/masked/ISR-blocked polls, SMM transitions, combined P/RR/RIS commands, one-read consumption, exact register effects and normal EOI. Ordinary status/IMR reads remain passive when no poll is armed.
- [ ] Test selection freezing with a newly arriving higher-priority request between OUT and IN, including initially empty polls. Verify later requests remain serviceable. Test controller/instance isolation and cancellation of an armed transaction by ICW1 and Machine reset.
- [ ] For both profiles, test slave propagation with IF clear, independent master/slave acknowledgement, separate EOIs, pending work across EOI ordering, and absence of phantom cascade delivery after draining requests. Preserve existing regular IRQ, priority, AEOI, cascade and CPU-shadow assertions.
- [ ] Add an original MIT assembly boot probe, offline preparation command `python3 tools/prepare_pic_poll_fixture.py`, and checked provenance manifest containing source/license, assembler command, source/boot/image hashes, exact results/guards and a maximum 2,000,000-slot budget per boot. Prepare it in acceptance CI before execution.
- [ ] The guest uses CLI and real port instructions to poll guest-programmed PIT and FDC READ ID requests, exercising master and slave acknowledgement, ISR/EOI results and an empty final poll. It subsequently demonstrates ordinary PIT IRQ delivery. Guest code computes and checks its own results; hosts never patch PIC state or result memory.
- [ ] Native tests and production release-Wasm browser tests boot the identical probe in VM and Ap, before/after reset, at both existing browser serving roots. Require guest PASS, exact complete result/guard bytes, unchanged disk bytes, no FAIL/core/browser errors and completion within the recorded budget.
- [ ] The Coordinator runs `cargo test --locked --test pic`, `cargo test --locked`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, `git diff --check`, and `npm test` after the existing README prerequisites and new fixture preparation. Preserve existing hardware, CPU, DOS/application, VM and six-game assertions and budgets. Use original/licensed source-built fixtures with explicit provenance; acquire no commercial ROMs or guest software.
- [ ] Update hardware/compatibility documentation and validation evidence with exact supported sequences, deterministic policies, remaining PIC scope and actual command outcomes. Review the complete diff against this Issue before merge. Limited acceptance must not be presented as full hardware accuracy or commercial compatibility.

## Optional validation

None.

None.
